title: Resonance Structures Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Mix blue paint with yellow and you get green. Milk in tea makes one new colour. A mix is not a switch. Diya drew ozone with one double bond and one single bond, so one side should be short and one side long. But both bonds are the same length. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we see why one drawing is not enough for some molecules.

On the molecule bench, an electron pair slides across ozone to turn drawing I into drawing II, then the real molecule settles at 128 pm for both bonds, between 121 pm (double) and 148 pm (single): the resonance hybrid. The double bond hops around the carbonate ion to give three canonical structures with three equal C-O bonds, we see why the hybrid is more stable, and CO2 at 115 pm. A worked example finds the carbonate bond order (4 / 3 = 1.33), then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 44 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
